## Testing Conventions

### Use Existing Fixtures
Prefer using existing fixtures over creating new records in tests. For example, use `leaves(:welcome_page)` instead of `books(:handbook).press Page.new(body: "..."), title: "..."`.

### URL Helpers in Tests
Use `_path` helpers instead of `_url` helpers in controller/integration tests unless you need to test across different hosts or explicitly need the full URL.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
get book_slug_path(books(:handbook))
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
get book_slug_url(books(:handbook))
```

### Response Body Assertions
Use `assert_in_body` and `assert_not_in_body` to check if text is present or absent in the response body without DOM manipulation.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
assert_in_body "Expected content"
assert_not_in_body "Unexpected content"
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
assert_includes response.body, "Expected content"
assert_not_includes response.body, "Unexpected content"
```

## Controller Conventions

### Simplified respond_to Blocks
When using `respond_to` with default rendering, omit the `{ render }` block as it's implied.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
def show
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html
    format.md
  end
end
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
def show
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html { render }
    format.md { render }
  end
end
```

      terms = remove_invalid_search_characters(terms)
      terms = remove_unbalanced_quotes(terms)
      terms.presence
    end

    def search(terms)
      if terms = sanitize_query_syntax(terms)

            "leaves.*",
            "highlight(leaf_search_index, 0, '<mark>', '</mark>') as title_match",
            "snippet(leaf_search_index, 1, '<mark>', '</mark>', '...', 20) as content_match")
      else
        none
      end
    end

    def with_search_results_for(terms)
      joins("join leaf_search_index on leaves.id = leaf_search_index.rowid")
        .where("leaf_search_index match ?", terms)
    end

  def reindex
    update_in_search_index if searchable?
  end

  def matches_for_highlight(terms)
    if terms = self.class.sanitize_query_syntax(terms)
      content = Leaf.with_search_results_for(terms)
        .where(id: id)
        .pick(Arel.sql("highlight(leaf_search_index, 1, '<mark>', '</mark>')"))

      content ? unique_matching_terms(content) : []
    end

    # This is a hygiene measure, not a security boundary — display-time
    # sanitization in sanitize_search_result is the primary defense.
    # ActionText content (Pages) is already HTML-safe plain text via
    # ERB::Util.html_escape, so skip it to avoid double-encoding.
    def sanitize_for_index(text)
      if text.html_safe?
        text
      else
        Rails::Html::FullSanitizer.new.sanitize(text)
      end
    end

    def create_in_search_index
      execute_sql_with_binds "insert into leaf_search_index(rowid, title, content ) values (?, ?, ?)",
        id, sanitize_for_index(title), sanitize_for_index(searchable_content)
    end

    def update_in_search_index
      transaction do
        updated = execute_sql_with_binds "update leaf_search_index set title = ?, content = ? where rowid = ?",
          sanitize_for_index(title), sanitize_for_index(searchable_content), id

        create_in_search_index unless updated
      end
    end

    def remove_from_search_index
      execute_sql_with_binds "delete from leaf_search_index where rowid = ?", id
    end

    def execute_sql_with_binds(*statement)
      self.class.connection.execute self.class.sanitize_sql(statement)

      self.class.connection.raw_connection.changes.nonzero?
    end

    def unique_matching_terms(content)
      terms = content.scan(/<mark>(.*?)<\/mark>/).flatten.uniq
      terms.sort_by(&:length).reverse
    end

    class_methods do
      private
        def remove_invalid_search_characters(terms)
          terms.gsub(/[^\w"]/, " ")
        end

        def remove_unbalanced_quotes(terms)
          if terms.count("\"").even?
            terms
          else
            terms.gsub("\"", " ")
          end

    end

module Authentication
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern
  include SessionLookup

  included do
    before_action :require_authentication
    helper_method :signed_in?

    protect_from_forgery with: :exception, unless: -> { authenticated_by.bot_key? }
  end

  class_methods do
    def require_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      allow_unauthenticated_access **options
      before_action :redirect_signed_in_user_to_root, **options
    end

    def allow_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_authentication, **options
      before_action :restore_authentication, **options
    end
  end

  private
    def signed_in?
      Current.user.present?
    end

    def require_authentication
      restore_authentication || request_authentication
    end

    def restore_authentication
      if session = find_session_by_cookie
        resume_session session
      end
    end

    def request_authentication
      session[:return_to_after_authenticating] = request.url
      redirect_to new_session_url
    end

    def redirect_signed_in_user_to_root
      redirect_to root_url if signed_in?
    end

    def start_new_session_for(user)
      user.sessions.start!(user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip).tap do |session|
        authenticated_as session
      end
    end

    def resume_session(session)
      session.resume user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip
      authenticated_as session
    end

    def terminate_current_session
      Current.session&.destroy!
      reset_session
      remove_authentication_cookie
    end

    def authenticated_as(session)
      Current.session = session
      set_authenticated_by(:session)
      set_authentication_cookie(session)
    end

    def post_authenticating_url
      session.delete(:return_to_after_authenticating) || root_url
    end

    def set_authentication_cookie(session)
      cookies.signed.permanent[:session_token] = { value: session.token, httponly: true, same_site: :lax }
    end

    def remove_authentication_cookie
      cookies.delete(:session_token)
    end

    def set_authenticated_by(method)
      @authenticated_by = method.to_s.inquiry
    end

    def authenticated_by
      @authenticated_by ||= "".inquiry
    end
end

require "test_helper"

class BookTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "slug is generated from title" do
    book = Book.create!(title: "Hello, World!")
    assert_equal "hello-world", book.slug
  end

  test "press a leafable" do

    assert leaf.page?
    assert_equal "Important words", leaf.page.body.content.to_s
    assert_equal "Introduction", leaf.title
  end

  test "markable combines all leafables" do
    leaves(:welcome_page).leafable.update!(body: "Welcome page content")
    leaves(:summary_page).leafable.update!(body: "Summary page content")

    assert_includes books(:handbook).markable, "Welcome page content"
    assert_includes books(:handbook).markable, "Summary page content"
  end

  test "markable joins leafables with double newlines" do

    leaves(:summary_page).leafable.update!(body: "Summary content")

    assert_not_includes books(:handbook).markable, leaves(:summary_page).title

require "test_helper"

class Book::AccessableTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "update_access always grants read access to everyone when everyone_access is set" do
    book = Book.create!(title: "My new book")
    book.update_access(editors: [], readers: [])

    assert book.everyone_access?

    User.all.each do |user|
      assert book.accessable?(user: user)
      assert_not book.editable?(user: user) unless user.administrator?
    end
  end

  test "update_access updates existing access" do
    book = Book.create!(title: "My new book", everyone_access: false)

    book.update_access(editors: [ users(:kevin).id ], readers: [])
    assert book.editable?(user: users(:kevin))

    book.update_access(editors: [], readers: [ users(:kevin).id ])
    assert book.accessable?(user: users(:kevin))
    assert_not book.editable?(user: users(:kevin))
  end

  test "update_access removes stale accesses" do
    book = Book.create!(title: "My new book", everyone_access: false)

    book.update_access(editors: [ users(:kevin).id ], readers: [ users(:jz).id ])
    assert_equal 2, book.accesses.size

    book.update_access(editors: [ users(:kevin).id ], readers: [])
    assert_equal 1, book.accesses.size
  end
end

ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
  alice = User.create!(name: "Alice", email_address: "alice@example.com", password: "secret")
  bob = User.create!(name: "Bob", email_address: "bob@example.com", password: "secret")

  # Session creates SignInEvent

  puts "SignInEvents after start: #{SignInEvent.for_address("alice@example.com").pluck(:action, :email_address)}"

  # Private book created by Alice
  Current.user = alice
  priv_book = Book.create!(title: "Alice Diary", author: "Alice", everyone_access: false)
  priv_book.update_access(editors: [alice.id], readers: [bob.id])

  # Shared book created by Alice
  shared_book = Book.create!(title: "Shared Guide", author: "Alice", everyone_access: true)
  shared_book.update_access(editors: [alice.id], readers: [])

  # Leaves in private book
  page_leaf = priv_book.press(Page.new(body: "Secret xylophone diary"), title: "Diary Page 1")
  page_leaf.reindex
  # Edit page leaf to create an Edit revision!
  page_leaf.edit(leafable_params: { body: "Updated secret xylophone diary" })
  section_leaf = priv_book.press(Section.new(body: "Secret section zzz"), title: "Secret Section")
  section_leaf.reindex
  # Trashen a leaf
  trashed_leaf = priv_book.press(Page.new(body: "Trashed secret qqq"), title: "Trashed Page")
  trashed_leaf.reindex
  trashed_leaf.trashed!

  # Reading marks
  ReadingMark.remember(page_leaf, user: alice)
  ReadingMark.remember(page_leaf, user: bob)
  shared_leaf = shared_book.press(Page.new(body: "Public guide content"), title: "Guide 1")
  shared_leaf.reindex
  ReadingMark.remember(shared_leaf, user: alice)
  ReadingMark.remember(shared_leaf, user: bob)

  puts "FTS rows before destroy: #{ActiveRecord::Base.connection.select_all("select rowid, title, content from leaf_search_index").to_a}"

  puts "Markdowns still existing for those pages: #{ActionText::Markdown.where(record_type: "Page", record_id: priv_page_ids).pluck(:id, :record_id, :content)}"
  puts "FTS rows after priv_book.destroy (still in tx): #{ActiveRecord::Base.connection.select_all("select rowid, title, content from leaf_search_index").to_a}"

  raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
end
'

**Comprehensive Search Index Cleanup Investigation**

Okay, here's what I'm thinking, based on this code and these scenarios. We've got a critical issue brewing with how we're handling search index cleanup, specifically regarding `leaf_search_index`.

First off, it seems clear that simply destroying a `Book` (with its `has_many :leaves, dependent: :destroy`) *should* trigger the necessary cleanup through `after_destroy_commit :remove_from_search_index`, thanks to the cascading deletes. But *how* is this handled? We need to verify this properly.

What I'm worried about is **Case 1**: If we use `book.leaves.delete_all` or similar bulk delete operations that bypass the ActiveRecord callbacks, we're going to leave stale entries in `leaf_search_index`. That's a huge problem. This should be added to a test.

**And then Case 2, which is potentially bigger**: We need to understand the behavior when a `Leaf` is destroyed and its `leafable` is a `Section` whose `body` attribute has been updated to `nil`, OR if the `leafable` isn't fully loaded at the time of destruction, or if the `leafable` has been already destroyed. The implications of this are significant.

Specifically, I'm concerned about the `if: :searchable?` condition in our `after_destroy_commit` callback, and how it behaves when the associated `Section`'s `body` is set to `nil`. If this evaluates to false, our cleanup *won't* run, leaving stale entries. This is worth a dedicated test. This is an absolutely huge potential issue.

What happens if `leaf_search_index` is checked inside a transaction, such as with `use_transactional_tests = true`? We've got to run tests in both `ActiveSupport::TestCase` (with transactional fixtures) and `ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest` to see what actually gets flushed when `book.destroy` or `user.destroy` occurs.

Then, there's the `Leaf::Editable` module and its `record_moved_to_trash` method. This creates an `Edit` row that *also* points to the same `Page` or `Section`. And if we've switched `has_many :edits, dependent: :delete_all` to `dependent: :destroy`, we're potentially in a very delicate situation with cascading destroys, and we must test this in detail. What happens when a leaf is "trashed" (marked for deletion) but not yet *actually* destroyed, and how does this affect the search index? `Books::SearchesController` filters based on `@book.leaves.active.search(...)`, meaning that trashed leaves don't appear in the book search. However, what *remains* in `leaf_search_index` is the actual issue.

And ultimately, what's the point of the `if: :searchable?` on `after_destroy_commit`? Deleting a non-existent index row is a no-op, meaning it's completely harmless. *But*, this conditional is only introducing a potential bug if `searchable_content` becomes null, or if `leafable` is already destroyed. I need to be sure the blobs are gone.

I need to nail this down. So, I need to ensure that the process of collecting blob IDs *before* destroying records, and then purging them *synchronously* in an `after_destroy_commit` callback, is robust, particularly inside a test transaction, where callbacks can behave differently. Wait, *do* these callbacks run immediately inside a test transaction? I've got to confirm that, because if `after_destroy_commit` isn't reliable in a transaction, the whole strategy falls apart! Specifically, I need to test that `after_destroy_commit` fires after the inner transaction on the *destroyed* records.

Now, Layer C: `Leaf::Searchable` and the FTS5 index. I need to scrutinize every line of `app/models/leaf/searchable.rb`.  I see some serious potential bugs here. First, that conditional `if: :searchable?` on `remove_from_search_index` is a HUGE red flag. What if `searchable_content` is now `nil` after the `leaf` is destroyed?  The index won't be cleaned up, and I can't have that! Even worse, if `searchable_content` has to be called on a leafable that is *also* destroyed, it's a guaranteed crash. I need to remove that conditional! It must *always* remove from the index.

Also, I'm concerned about the timing of `remove_from_search_index`. Should it be `after_destroy` or `after_destroy_commit`? I need to think about transactions and how SQLite FTS5 behaves. The FTS index is in the *same* database as the application data, so an `after_destroy` hook means this deletion is *atomic* with the main record. If the transaction rolls back, the FTS row is restored. If the transaction commits, the FTS row is already gone, no stale search hits!

I'm thinking about fixtures and tests!  I also need to check how they load the fixtures directly into `leaves` without running `after_create_commit` and whether I need to ensure that I reindex the data in a testing scenario. And what about updates, with `after_update_commit :update_in_search_index, if: :searchable?`? If the body is cleared out, it won't be removed! I need a more reliable solution.

What about legacy data? With the old code, deactivated users, their private books, their leaves, and their `leaf_search_index` rows are still lurking. Now that I have this erasure strategy, I'm going to eliminate *all* of those rows.  I need to verify that FTS index doesn't have any stale data from destroyed books. The FTS index doesn't store author names or user names, so I don't need to worry about that.

Finally, I need to verify how `Leaf::Searchable.search` itself works. If a leaf is deleted, but its `rowid` remains in the index, a direct SQL query would still return stale data from a *deleted* user! Even worse, I could have an ID collision when a new leaf reuses the deleted ID, leading to a unique constraint violation and even returning data from a different user!  It makes the deletion on *every* leaf destroy absolutely critical!

I'm now going to verify the FTS5 deletion in a transaction to make sure that it rolls back, testing the "optional" associations, and testing on the edits. I need to test this *now*.

**GDPR Erasure Implementation Review**

Okay, let's break this down. The core issue is ensuring complete and correct data erasure when a user is destroyed, handling all related dependencies and avoiding `ActiveRecord::InvalidForeignKey` errors. My thought process is to systematically analyze the existing relationships, identify potential pitfalls, and then implement the necessary changes in a clean, step-by-step manner.

First, I identified the cascade problem with the destroy logic. It wasn't failing in the repro because shared and private books were destroyed, cascading reading_marks. If a reading mark had been kept, the destroy would have crashed. We also found orphaned records that needed to be cleaned up.

The proposed solution focuses on a new `User::Erasable` concern, which encapsulates the GDPR erasure logic. We're going to use `before_destroy` callbacks to prepare for the erasure and `after_destroy_commit` to purge all related data.

Specifically, the * `before_destroy :prepare_erasure, prepend: true` * callback does the following:
  *   Collects all of the relevant blob IDs for later deletion, specifically those related to private books ( `everyone_access: false` ).
  *   Anonymizes shared books ( `everyone_access: true` ) by assigning the creator to `nil` and setting the author to `Deleted author`
  *   Destroys all private books to remove their associated resources.

Then, *`after_destroy :erase_sign_in_events`* takes care of deleting all `SignInEvent` records associated with the user, using either the persisted email address or what was modified to it in memory, or the original email address, ensuring it handles both active and previously deactivated user entries. This is where we need to be very careful to use the database email address, or fall back to the in-memory email if necessary to ensure correctness (and also the original, if applicable).

Lastly,  `*after_destroy_commit :purge_erased_blobs`* synchronously purges the collected blobs. This is done after the transaction to prevent foreign key errors.

We must make several specific model changes:

*   The `Book` model needs `dependent: :destroy` on certain associations to cascade the deletes properly. This ensures that when a private book is destroyed, all related data, like leaves, edits, attachments, etc., is also destroyed.
*   We're switching the `dependent: :destroy` to `dependent: :purge_later` on the `uploads` association within `ActionText::RichText` for attachments.
*   We need to change `dependent: :delete_all` for some associations, like `reading_marks` and `sessions`, to prevent triggering `before_destroy` callbacks on related models (like those to delete `SignInEvent`s). We're going to delete all user's sessions to avoid triggering `Session::Auditable#record_signed_out`.
*   We will delete `reading_marks` associated with the user, both those on other books and the user's remaining marks, to prevent foreign key errors.
*   We should update the `User` to include the `Authoring`, `Erasable`, `Role`, and `Transferable` concerns.
*   We'll use scopes like `deactivated` on the `User` model, to differentiate active from deactivated users in our views.
*   The `UsersController` will be updated to handle the `destroy` action more thoroughly, including the correct user lookup using `User.find(params[:id])` and a different `deactivate` action for now.

module Leaf::Editable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS = 10.minutes

  included do
    has_many :edits, dependent: :destroy

    after_update :record_moved_to_trash, if: :was_trashed?
  end

  def edit(leafable_params: {}, leaf_params: {})
    if record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      update_and_record_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    else
      update_without_recording_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    end
  end

  private
    def record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      will_change_leafable?(leafable_params) && last_edit_old?
    end

    def last_edit_old?
      edits.empty? || edits.last.created_at.before?(MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS.ago)
    end

    def will_change_leafable?(leafable_params)
      leafable_params.select do |key, value|
        leafable.attributes[key.to_s] != value
      end.present?
    end

    def update_without_recording_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.last&.touch
        update! leaf_params
      end
    end

    def update_and_record_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        new_leafable = dup_leafable_with_attachments leafable
        new_leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.revision.create!(leafable: leafable)
        update! leaf_params.merge(leafable: new_leafable)
      end
    end

    def dup_leafable_with_attachments(leafable)
      leafable.dup.tap do |new|
        leafable.attachment_reflections.each do |name, _|
          new.send(name).attach(leafable.send(name).blob)
        end
      end
    end

    def record_moved_to_trash
      edits.trash.create!(leafable: leafable)
    end

    def was_trashed?
      trashed? && previous_changes.include?(:status)
    end
end
EOF

module Leaf::Searchable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit :create_in_search_index, if: :searchable?
    after_update_commit :update_in_search_index
    after_destroy       :remove_from_search_index

    end

    def sanitize_query_syntax(terms)
      terms = terms.to_s
      terms = remove_invalid_search_characters(terms)
      terms = remove_unbalanced_quotes(terms)
      terms.presence
    end

    def search(terms)
      if terms = sanitize_query_syntax(terms)
        with_search_results_for(terms)
          .select(
            "leaves.*",
            "highlight(leaf_search_index, 0, '<mark>', '</mark>') as title_match",
            "snippet(leaf_search_index, 1, '<mark>', '</mark>', '...', 20) as content_match")
      else
        none
      end
    end

    def with_search_results_for(terms)
      joins("join leaf_search_index on leaves.id = leaf_search_index.rowid")
        .where("leaf_search_index match ?", terms)
    end
  end

  def reindex
    update_in_search_index if searchable?
  end

    if terms = self.class.sanitize_query_syntax(terms)
      content = Leaf.with_search_results_for(terms)
        .where(id: id)
        .pick(Arel.sql("highlight(leaf_search_index, 1, '<mark>', '</mark>')"))

      content ? unique_matching_terms(content) : []
    end
  end

  private
    def searchable?
      searchable_content
    end

    # Strip tags from content before indexing to keep the FTS table clean.
    # This is a hygiene measure, not a security boundary — display-time
    # sanitization in sanitize_search_result is the primary defense.
    # ActionText content (Pages) is already HTML-safe plain text via
    # ERB::Util.html_escape, so skip it to avoid double-encoding.
    def sanitize_for_index(text)
      if text.html_safe?
        text
      else
        Rails::Html::FullSanitizer.new.sanitize(text)
      end
    end

    def create_in_search_index
      execute_sql_with_binds "insert into leaf_search_index(rowid, title, content ) values (?, ?, ?)",
        id, sanitize_for_index(title), sanitize_for_index(searchable_content)
    end

    def update_in_search_index
      if searchable?
        transaction do
          updated = execute_sql_with_binds "update leaf_search_index set title = ?, content = ? where rowid = ?",
            sanitize_for_index(title), sanitize_for_index(searchable_content), id

          create_in_search_index unless updated
        end
      else
        remove_from_search_index
      end
    end

    def remove_from_search_index
      execute_sql_with_binds "delete from leaf_search_index where rowid = ?", id
    end

    def execute_sql_with_binds(*statement)
      self.class.connection.execute self.class.sanitize_sql(statement)

      self.class.connection.raw_connection.changes.nonzero?
    end

    def unique_matching_terms(content)
      terms = content.scan(/<mark>(.*?)<\/mark>/).flatten.uniq
      terms.sort_by(&:length).reverse
    end

    class_methods do
      private
        def remove_invalid_search_characters(terms)
          terms.gsub(/[^\w"]/, " ")
        end

        def remove_unbalanced_quotes(terms)
          if terms.count("\"").even?
            terms
          else
            terms.gsub("\"", " ")
          end
        end
    end
end

I need to make sure this logic is robust to different scenarios. Remember the case where someone deactivates a user, and the email gets munged, like `"alice-deactivated-<UUID>@example.com"`? The current implementation uses a UUID pattern and a fallback, but I have to ensure the regexes don't cause unexpected results.

I'm playing with edge cases where the `active` attribute might be `false`, and the email address is altered, either via UUID, or manually. The primary concern is if the pattern matching and substitution are behaving as expected to get the *original* email address back. It's crucial that we always derive the correct original email address, even if someone messes with the format in a test.

Then I'm thinking about how `prepare_erasure` interacts with the database state. This runs *before* destruction and it's responsible for gathering all the email addresses and blob IDs. The *key* is it runs before the actual destruction happens, meaning `email_address_in_database` and `active_in_database` are still available when we're calculating those email addresses. That's a clean and safe design.

The method `sign_in_email_addresses` is quite elegant, it just grabs the database address (if it exists) or the current one and passes it to `original_email_address`. Then it does a `compact.uniq` to remove duplicates.

The blob ID collection logic in `collect_private_book_blob_ids` is really important too. We have to be sure it correctly finds all the associated data – private books, leaves, pages, pictures, markdown, and their associated ActiveStorage blobs, both primary and variants. I am particularly careful with the blob ID logic to get every single id, which are then passed to the purge process.

One more thing to consider: the destruction lifecycle in ActiveRecord, and how this all plays out within a database transaction. `prepare_erasure` runs *before_destroy*, which is *inside* the transaction. The deletion happens after that, so that process is safe. The erasure of sign-in events happen in `after_destroy`, still *inside* the transaction, and the `purge_erased_blobs` run in `after_destroy_commit`. The `after_destroy_commit` is *outside* the transaction (it is run right after it is committed), this is key to protect against rollbacks in case of exceptions. That means we don't end up deleting disk files if the transaction rolls back. In regular use (e.g., calling `user.destroy!`), the transaction commits immediately before `destroy!` returns, so this all happens synchronously.

But immediately afterward, with `alice.destroy!`, everything appears to be cleaned up: no blobs, attachments, variant records, or files on disk. And the `perform_enqueued_jobs` runs without a hitch. This is excellent! But I need to be *absolutely* sure.

The next thing I think to check is to make sure this behavior is consistent whether running inside a Rails `ActiveSupport::TestCase` or an `ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest`, since they interact with transactions differently. It's critical that `after_destroy_commit :purge_erased_blobs` runs immediately in *both* contexts.

I'm going to remove that temporary file (`tmp/repro_gdpr.rb`) and write a solid suite of tests. I'll stick very closely to the conventions outlined in `AGENTS.md` - use fixtures, helper methods, and modern assertion methods.

Here's the plan: I need to write some comprehensive tests. I'm going to create four distinct test files:

1.  **`test/models/user/erasable_test.rb`**: This will cover the model unit tests, really digging into every single edge case. I need to make sure erasing an active user deletes everything related to them: user row, sessions, events, accesses, reading marks, *and* their private books (including all associated data like leaves, edits, pages, sections, pictures, markdown, attachments, blobs, variants, FTS entries). But the shared books should be handled carefully. I need to be sure that they are *preserved*, but the creator ID is set to `nil`, author to "Deleted author", and the erased user's accesses and reading marks are removed. I'll need to check the behavior when erasing a previously deactivated user, and ensure emails are handled correctly. Error conditions are important, such as a user with an email that might include `-deactivated-`. Lastly, I'll need to confirm that `perform_enqueued_jobs` runs without error after the erasure and verify that a user can be re-created with the same credentials.

2.  **`test/controllers/users_controller_test.rb`**: Controller and integration tests are critical. I'll test the `/users/:id` `destroy` action, verifying that the user count decreases, that the correct objects are deleted, that private data is destroyed, and shared books are correctly anonymized. I'll need to check the erasure of deactivated users, and the handling of the original sign-in events. Session invalidation is another important item: I'll check that the old session cookie redirects to login and the old transfer link returns `:bad_request`. I need to be sure shared books remain readable and searchable after the erasure, with the correct "Deleted author" byline. Finally, I'll restrict this functionality to admins, ensuring that non-admins can't destroy users (active or deactivated).

3.  **`test/models/book/authorship_test.rb`** (or `test/models/book_test.rb`): Checking how the `creator` is handled is very important. I need to ensure that the book creator is correctly set upon creation and persists the expected data even after `anonymize_author` and subsequent updates.

4.  **`test/models/leaf/searchable_test.rb` & `test/models/leaf/editable_test.rb`**: The last tests should ensure that the FTS index is correctly updated when leaves are destroyed, including edge cases like sections with cleared bodies or trashed leaves. Furthermore, revisions and trashed leafable data must be correctly cleaned up.

I'll start writing those tests *now*. This comprehensive approach should leave no doubt.

require "test_helper"

class UsersControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    @join_code = accounts(:signal).join_code
  end

  test "new" do
    get join_path(@join_code)
    assert_response :success
  end

  test "new does not allow a signed in user" do
    sign_in :david

    get join_path(@join_code)
    assert_redirected_to root_url
  end

  test "new requires a join code" do
    get join_path("not")
    assert_response :not_found
  end

  test "create" do
    assert_difference -> { User.count }, 1 do
      post join_path(@join_code), params: { user: { name: "New Person", email_address: "new@example.com", password: "secret123456" } }
    end

    assert_redirected_to root_url

    user = User.last
    assert_equal user.id, Session.find_by(token: parsed_cookies.signed[:session_token]).user.id
  end

  test "creating a new user with an existing email address redirects to login screen" do
    assert_no_difference -> { User.count } do
      post join_path(@join_code), params: { user: { name: "Another David", email_address: users(:david).email_address, password: "secret123456" } }
    end

    assert_redirected_to new_session_url(email_address: users(:david).email_address)
  end

  test "index shows deactivated users with remove button to admins only" do
    kevin = users(:kevin)
    kevin.deactivate

    sign_in :david
    get users_path
    assert_response :success
    assert_in_body kevin.name
    assert_select "form[action='#{user_path(kevin)}'] input[name='_method'][value='delete']"

    sign_out
    sign_in :jz
    get users_path
    assert_response :success
    assert_not_in_body kevin.name
  end

  test "update" do
    sign_in :david
    assert users(:david).administrator?

    put user_path(users(:kevin)), params: { user: { role: "administrator" } }

    assert_redirected_to users_url
    assert users(:kevin).reload.administrator?
  end

  test "update does not allow non-admins to change roles" do
    sign_in :kevin
    assert_not users(:kevin).administrator?

    put user_path(users(:kevin)), params: { user: { role: "administrator" } }

    assert_response :forbidden
    assert_not users(:kevin).reload.administrator?
  end

  test "destroy erases the user and their data while preserving everyone-access books" do
    kevin = users(:kevin)

    kevin.sessions.start!(user_agent: "TestBrowser", ip_address: "10.0.0.1")
    ReadingMark.remember(leaves(:welcome_page), user: kevin)

    Current.user = kevin
    private_book = Book.create!(title: "Kevin Secret", author: "Kevin", everyone_access: false)
    private_book.update_access(editors: [ kevin.id ], readers: [])
    private_leaf = private_book.press(Page.new(body: "Confidential pangolin"), title: "Secret")

    shared_book = Book.create!(title: "Public Handbook", author: "Kevin", everyone_access: true)
    shared_book.update_access(editors: [ kevin.id ], readers: [])
    shared_leaf = shared_book.press(Page.new(body: "Helpful koala guide"), title: "Getting Started")

    sign_in :david

    assert_difference -> { User.count }, -1 do
      delete user_path(kevin)
    end

    assert_redirected_to users_url
    assert_nil User.find_by(id: kevin.id)
    assert_empty Session.where(user_id: kevin.id)
    assert_empty SignInEvent.for_address(kevin.email_address)
    assert_empty Access.where(user_id: kevin.id)
    assert_empty ReadingMark.where(user_id: kevin.id)
    assert_not Book.exists?(private_book.id)
    assert_empty ActiveRecord::Base.connection.select_all("select rowid from leaf_search_index where rowid = #{private_leaf.id}").to_a

    # Shared book keeps working with "Deleted author" byline
    shared_book.reload
    assert_nil shared_book.creator_id
    assert_equal "Deleted author", shared_book.author

    get root_path
    assert_response :success
    assert_in_body "Public Handbook"
    assert_in_body "Deleted author"
    assert_not_in_body "Kevin Secret"

    get book_slug_path(shared_book)
    assert_response :success
    assert_in_body "Deleted author"
    assert_not_in_body "Kevin"

    get book_slug_path(shared_book, format: :md)
    assert_response :success
    assert_in_body 'author: "Deleted author"'

    get leafable_slug_path(shared_leaf)
    assert_response :success
    assert_in_body "Helpful koala guide"
    assert_in_body "Deleted author"

    post book_search_path(shared_book), params: { search: "koala" }
    assert_response :success
    assert_in_body "Getting Started"
  end

  test "destroy erases a previously deactivated user and their original sign-in events" do
    kevin = users(:kevin)
    original_email = kevin.email_address

    kevin.sessions.start!(user_agent: "TestBrowser", ip_address: "10.0.0.1")
    ReadingMark.remember(leaves(:welcome_page), user: kevin)

    Current.user = kevin

    shared_book = Book.create!(title: "Old Shared Book", author: "Kevin", everyone_access: true)
    shared_book.update_access(editors: [ kevin.id ], readers: [])

    kevin.deactivate
    assert_not kevin.active?
    assert_equal 1, SignInEvent.for_address(original_email).count

    sign_in :david

    assert_difference -> { User.count }, -1 do
      delete user_path(kevin)
    end

    assert_redirected_to users_url
    assert_nil User.find_by(id: kevin.id)
    assert_empty SignInEvent.for_address(original_email)
    assert_empty SignInEvent.for_address(kevin.email_address)
    assert_empty Access.where(user_id: kevin.id)
    assert_empty ReadingMark.where(user_id: kevin.id)
    assert_not Book.exists?(private_book.id)
    assert_empty ActiveRecord::Base.connection.select_all("select rowid from leaf_search_index where rowid = #{private_leaf.id}").to_a

    shared_book.reload
    assert_nil shared_book.creator_id
    assert_equal "Deleted author", shared_book.author

    get users_path
    assert_response :success
    assert_not_in_body kevin.name
  end

  test "destroy invalidates erased user's active session, transfer link, and sign-in" do
    kevin = users(:kevin)
    transfer_id = kevin.transfer_id

    # Capture Kevin's active session cookie
    sign_in :kevin
    kevin_session_cookie = cookies[:session_token]

    # Admin erases Kevin
    sign_in :david
    delete user_path(kevin)
    assert_redirected_to users_url

    # Kevin's old session cookie no longer works
    cookies[:session_token] = kevin_session_cookie
    get users_path
    assert_redirected_to new_session_url

    # Kevin's transfer link and password login no longer work
    put session_transfer_path(transfer_id)
    assert_response :bad_request

    post session_path, params: { email_address: kevin.email_address, password: "secret123456" }
    assert_response :unauthorized
  end

  test "destroy is not allowed to non-admins" do
    sign_in :kevin

    assert_no_difference -> { User.count } do
      delete user_path(users(:david))
    end
    assert_response :forbidden

    users(:jz).deactivate
    assert_no_difference -> { User.count } do
      delete user_path(users(:jz))
    end
    assert_response :forbidden
  end
end
